metadata.short_desc: One sentence in, a picture out — models and workflows picked for you
metadata.desc: Connects AstrBot to ComfyUI: describe it in one sentence and get an image. The plugin detects the models and nodes actually installed in your ComfyUI, picks Checkpoint / LoRA / VAE on its own, and matches the right workflow template, resolution and sampling parameters for SD1.5 / SDXL / Pony / Flux and other architectures. Supports image-to-image, outpaint, inpainting (paint the mask in the settings page) and reverse-prompting from an image; with several ComfyUI instances it load-balances and circuit-breaks failing nodes. Generation progress streams over WebSocket and can be aborted with /cancel; text-to-video and image-to-video are supported (GGUF quantisation included, runs on 8G VRAM); UI and prompts are bilingual. Concurrent users are queued behind a concurrency gate. UI-format workflows can be imported directly. Supports custom API-format workflow templates, permissions and quotas, generation stats and a gallery. Results can be sent as a single forwarded message (QQ personal account) so multi-image runs no longer flood the chat. Also offers ControlNet depth control and upscaling (to an exact width/height); preprocessor weights that are downloaded on demand from HuggingFace are probed before submission, and fall back to image-to-image for composition preservation instead of failing halfway through.

t2i.hint: Enabled by default. The most basic generation capability.

i2i.hint: Disabled by default. Image-to-image is VRAM-hungry and could also be used to alter someone else's image, so enable it only as needed.

outpaint.hint: Disabled by default. Extends the canvas outwards; VRAM usage rises with the expansion amount.

inpaint.description: Inpaint (paint the mask in the config page)
inpaint.hint: Disabled by default. The “Inpaint” tab in the config page reports that it is unavailable while this is off.

t2v.hint: Disabled by default. Video is the most VRAM- and time-hungry feature (74–281 seconds per clip on an 8G machine); when off, /video does nothing and stays silent.

i2v.hint: Disabled by default. Makes a still image move; also VRAM-hungry.

reverse_prompt.hint: Disabled by default. Strictly speaking this is not a generation feature, but it calls a vision model too, so it is exposed as a switch as well; when off, /img2prompt does nothing and stays silent.

control.hint: Disabled by default. Attach a reference image + --control depth to constrain composition and pose with a depth map. Requires a ControlNet model (control-depth-sdxl-small-fp16) and the depth preprocessor weights (depth_anything_v2_vits.pth, in controlnet_aux's ckpts). Set strength with --control-strength (default 0.8) and the stop point with --control-end (default 0.7). ⚠️ The preprocessor weights are not under models/; they are downloaded from HuggingFace on demand, so if they are missing the job fails halfway through. The plugin probes before submitting and, if the probe fails, automatically falls back to image-to-image to preserve composition (denoise 0.45); use `/health --probe` to check manually.

upscale.hint: Disabled by default. `/upscale --scale 2` upscales with a 4x model and scales back down to the target factor (default 2, max 4); `/upscale --scale-to 1920x1088` outputs the exact width and height (use this when you need a fixed size); adding `--upscale 2` or `--upscale 1920x1088` to a generation upscales the result once automatically. Model: upscale_models/4x-UltraSharp.safetensors.

language.hint: auto=follow the AstrBot UI language (fall back to Chinese if unavailable). Chat text, LLM prompts and config-page navigation switch along with it. The text files live under .astrbot-plugin/i18n/ and can be extended yourself.

base_url.hint: An address reachable from AstrBot, for example http://127.0.0.1:8188

timeout.hint: Excludes queue time. When tasks are ahead in the queue, the wait is extended automatically.

max_tasks_ahead.hint: Each task ahead adds 60 seconds of compensation; this value caps how many tasks are counted, so one stuck task cannot cause an endless wait.

free_before_switch.description: Unload the previous set before switching to a large model
free_before_switch.hint: Before switching to a large model (SDXL / Flux / Lumina / Wan video, i.e. anything above 4GB), ask ComfyUI to unload the previous set first to free memory. Strongly recommended on 16G machines — measured: without unloading, loading a 6.5GB SDXL reports “paging file is too small, os error 1455” and makes ComfyUI crash. With it off, switching models skips the reload wait, but memory pressure can easily crash ComfyUI.

queue.description: Generation queue and concurrency (prevents several simultaneous generations from exhausting VRAM)

max_concurrent.hint: How many tasks may run in ComfyUI at once; the rest queue on the plugin side. 1 is recommended for a single GPU (ComfyUI itself executes them one by one); raise it with multiple GPUs or when ComfyUI has parallel execution enabled.

per_user_limit.hint: How many tasks one person may run at once; the rest go to the end of the queue, so one person cannot fill it by sending a dozen requests. 0 means unlimited.

wait_timeout.hint: How long a request may queue on the plugin side; on timeout it is clearly reported and the generation is cancelled instead of hanging silently. 0 means unlimited.

backends.description: Multi-backend scheduling (automatically distribute by load when several ComfyUI instances exist)

endpoints.hint: One per line, “address|name” is supported, for example http://192.168.1.20:8188|Line 2. The primary address is still the “server address” above. Leave empty = use only the primary backend.

strategy.hint: least_queue=send to whichever is idle (default); round_robin=rotate; primary=use only the primary backend.

fail_cooldown.hint: After a node fails submission or cannot be reached, no tasks are dispatched to it during this period. 0=no cooldown.

llm_settings.description: LLM settings (used to turn Chinese descriptions into prompts and to pick models)

enable_prompt_optimize.description: Enable prompt optimization and smart model selection
enable_prompt_optimize.hint: When off, your exact wording is used directly as the positive prompt and the first available checkpoint is used — no LLM needed at all. When on: Chinese descriptions are rewritten into English tags (faithful to the original, adding nothing you did not mention), and the checkpoint/LoRA is chosen by style; generic quality words and hand-avoidance words are added locally by the plugin, so the LLM does not write them twice.

provider.hint: Leave empty to use the current session's model (that is, AstrBot's default chat model). IDs can be viewed on AstrBot's “Service Providers” page.

base_url.hint: When filled, AstrBot's provider is no longer used and the plugin connects to this endpoint directly (for example https://api.openai.com/v1).

api_key.description: API key for the custom endpoint

model.description: Model name for the custom endpoint

optimize_for_video.description: Have the AI rewrite video prompts too
optimize_for_video.hint: When on, /video and /i2v first rewrite your description into a “video prompt”: filling in **motion** (slowly turning the head, gently swaying), **camera movement** (static/push-in/pan) and lighting mood, while keeping your original language (Chinese in, Chinese out — Wan natively understands Chinese). Unlike the image path — images stack English tags, video needs natural-language motion descriptions. The video model is decided by video.t2v_model / video.i2v_model; the LLM only rewrites the prompt and never picks models. Override per request in chat: --llm forces a rewrite, --no-llm skips it for this request.

vision_settings.description: Reverse-prompt model (used when reading an image to produce a prompt; same structure as the LLM settings above)

provider.hint: Recommended: add a vision-capable model in AstrBot “Service Providers” (such as qwen-vl-max, glm-4v, gpt-4o) and fill its ID in here. Leave empty to use the current session's chat model.

base_url.hint: Once filled, the provider above is no longer used and the plugin connects to this endpoint directly (for example https://dashscope.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1).

api_key.description: API key for the custom endpoint

model.description: Model name for the custom endpoint
model.hint: Must be a vision-capable model, for example qwen-vl-max.

override_arch_defaults.description: Force the parameters below (ignore automatic architecture adaptation)
override_arch_defaults.hint: When off: the plugin selects the correct resolution, CFG and sampler automatically by checkpoint architecture (SD1.5/SDXL/Pony/Flux); the values below are only a fallback when the architecture is not recognized.

arch_override.hint: Leave empty = detect from the file name (containing xl means SDXL, pony/illustrious means Pony, flux means Flux, otherwise SD1.5). Fill in one of sd15 / sdxl / pony / flux / sd3 when detection is wrong.

add_quality_tags.description: Add quality words automatically by architecture
add_quality_tags.hint: When on, positive prompts for SD1.5/Pony models automatically carry quality words (not added for SDXL/Flux — adding them can make results worse).

quality_words_by.hint: plugin=the plugin adds them by checkpoint architecture (default: masterpiece for SD1.5, score_9 for Pony, nothing for Flux); llm=also let the AI write 2–4 image-related quality words itself in the prompt (the plugin's generic words are still merged in, duplicates removed automatically). To leave it entirely to the AI, turn off “Add quality words automatically by architecture” above.

completion_mode.hint: strict=follow instructions exactly (default): only what you described is drawn, the AI adds no characters/clothing/props/scenes; commission=commission mode: the AI may add 1–3 **presentation-layer** details (light direction and texture, material texture, composition and depth of field, mood), but must not change the subject count/appearance/clothing style/actions/scene type, and it lists “what the AI added” in the result. Override once with /draw … --commission or --strict.

commission_params.description: Release sampling parameters as well in commission mode
commission_params.hint: Off by default. When on, in commission mode gentle adjustments are made if you did not specify parameters explicitly: CFG ×0.85 for the SD family (not below 1.5), guidance −1.0 for the Flux family (not below 1.0). Inline --cfg and the configured defaults always take priority.

negative_mode.hint: merge=merge everything (default words + hand-avoidance words + architecture words + LLM words, the most stable); guard_only=your words + hand-avoidance words, ignoring the LLM's negative words; custom_only=only your own words, deduplicated automatically; raw=exactly as given, not even deduplicated. Inline --negative merges under merge/guard_only/custom_only and overrides directly under raw.

force_vae.hint: Leave empty = use the checkpoint's built-in VAE. If images come out with a color cast or washed out, fill in the full VAE file name to correct it (put the VAE into ComfyUI's models/vae first).

default_negative.hint: Negative prompts are not used for the Flux architecture. Keeping it short and putting the most important words first is recommended; duplicates are removed automatically (((x)) and x count as the same word).

hires.description: Hires Fix (generate small, then upscale and redraw)

enable.description: Enable Hires Fix automatically for text-to-image
enable.hint: Every /draw (text-to-image) automatically goes through an upscale-and-redraw pass. One of the most effective ways to improve hands, faces and detail, but it roughly doubles generation time.

enable_for_i2i.description: Enable Hires Fix automatically for image-to-image too
enable_for_i2i.hint: Only takes effect together with “Enable Hires Fix automatically for text-to-image” above; to use Hires for image-to-image only, enable this option and disable the text-to-image one above, then use inline --hires (per-request override must be allowed).

allow_inline.description: Allow per-request overrides of Hires settings
allow_inline.hint: When on, users can send /draw description --hires 2.0 or --hires 0 themselves; when off, the configuration above always applies (so nobody can blow up VRAM with a large factor).

scale.hint: 1.5 is a common compromise; 2.0 is sharper but slower and uses more VRAM.

denoise.hint: 0.4–0.6 is typical: too low gains little detail, too high changes the composition.

steps.description: Second-pass steps (0 = same as the first pass)

i2i.description: Image-to-image (redraw based on the image you send, following your description)

enable.description: Use image-to-image automatically when /draw includes an image
enable.hint: When off, an attached image is handled as text-to-image; /i2i can still be called explicitly.

denoise.hint: Measured guidance: 0.30–0.40 changes details only, 0.40–0.50 keeps composition and color, 0.55–0.65 starts changing the art style, above 0.70 is close to a full redraw. Inline --denoise overrides a single request, and you can pass several tiers at once to compare directly (--denoise 0.4,0.55,0.7, sorted ascending with duplicates removed, max 4 tiers).

max_side.description: Max long side of the input image (pixels)
max_side.hint: Larger images are scaled down proportionally so a big image cannot exhaust VRAM; 0 means unlimited.

subfolder.description: Subdirectory to upload into ComfyUI input
subfolder.hint: Placed under input/astrbot by default, so your input root directory stays clean.

default_seconds.hint: Used when --seconds is not given. The Wan family handles native pacing automatically: with nothing specified it uses 81 frames (24fps ≈ 3.4 seconds); with only --seconds given, the frame count is converted at 24fps. Video is much slower than images — the official example is 121 frames / 5 seconds.

default_fps.hint: Only applies to non-Wan video models. The Wan family is trained at 24fps and automatically uses 24fps — rendering at 8–16fps and playing at normal speed turns into “a blurry image that barely moves” (learned from real testing). To force slow motion, write --fps inline. Frame counts are aligned to 4n+1 automatically.

max_seconds.hint: Requests beyond this are truncated to it with a note in the log, so nobody can ask for 60 seconds and blow up VRAM. 0=unlimited.

send_video.description: Send the video directly to the chat
send_video.hint: When off, only the local save path is given in the chat (use this on platforms that cannot send videos).

machine.hint: The tier caps resolution/frames/steps so low-end machines do not get overwhelmed. auto=decided by VRAM (≤10G→low, 12–20G→mid, ≥24G→high; with RAM <20G drop one tier). Low-end example: 8G VRAM/16G RAM → 480p, ≤97 frames, distilled models ≤12 steps; standard example: 12–20G VRAM/32G RAM → 720p, ≤121 frames, ≤30 steps; high-end example: ≥24G VRAM/64G RAM → 720p, ≤161 frames, ≤50 steps. To exceed the caps, pick a higher tier manually (whether it can run is your responsibility).

t2v_model.hint: Used when --model is not given (fill in the file name; a partial keyword is enough). Leave empty = automatically pick the first video weights. Low-end recommendation: Wan2_2-TI2V-5B-Turbo-Q4_K_M.gguf (fast) or Wan2.2-TI2V-5B-Q4_K_M.gguf (quality); standard recommendation: wan2.2_ti2v_5B_fp16.safetensors. Put models in diffusion_models/ or unet_gguf/.

i2v_model.hint: Used when --model is not given. Wan 2.2 TI2V-5B shares one model for text-to-video and image-to-video, so both entries can be the same on low-end setups; if you have separate I2V weights (such as wan2.2_i2v_* or Wan2.1 I2V), fill that in instead. Leave empty = auto-pick.

mention_trigger_user.description: Mention the triggering user when generating in a group chat

show_params.description: Attach parameter info to the image
show_params.hint: Shows the template name, checkpoint, resolution, seed and elapsed time, making results easy to reproduce.

merge_forward.description: Merge into a single forwarded message
merge_forward.hint: Packs the parameter text and images into **a single “merged forward” message**, so generating several images no longer floods the chat (QQ personal account / OneBot v11 only). ⚠️ Images are embedded as base64, so three cases fall back to normal sending automatically: the platform is not aiocqhttp, the result is a video, or the total image size exceeds 20MB.

merge_forward_name.hint: The sender nickname shown in the merged forward card; leave empty to use “ComfyUI Smart Drawing”.

show_progress.hint: Shows “step n / total steps” via ComfyUI's WebSocket push. If the WebSocket cannot connect it falls back to polling automatically, without affecting generation. When off, results are sent only on completion.

progress_interval.hint: Step events are very dense (one per step); they are throttled to this interval to avoid flooding. 0 means no throttling.

keep_images.hint: Beyond this, the oldest images are deleted by time so the disk does not fill up. 0 means no count-based cleanup.

image_max_age_days.hint: Images older than this are deleted. 0 means no time-based cleanup.

permission.description: Permissions and quotas (admin identity follows AstrBot's built-in administrator setting)

whitelist_user_ids.hint: Leave empty for no restriction. Only users in the list (and administrators) may generate images.

blacklist_user_ids.hint: The blacklist has the highest priority, administrators included.

daily_limit.hint: 0 means unlimited. Counts are written to disk and are not reset by a restart.

admin_bypass.description: Administrators bypass the whitelist, cooldown and quotas

feature_rules.hint:
One rule per line; lines starting with `#` are comments. Format:
user:123456=t2i,i2v ← this user may use text-to-image and image-to-video
group:987654=t2i   ← this group may only use text-to-image
default=t2i,i2i    ← features available to everyone else
Feature names: t2i / i2i / outpaint / inpaint / t2v / i2v / reverse_prompt; you may also write all (everything) or none (all disabled).
Priority: user > group > default > the “Feature switches” above. Administrators are not restricted here while “bypass” is on.
Leave empty = everyone follows the global feature switches.

video_daily_limit.description: Daily video limit per user (0 = unlimited)
video_daily_limit.hint: A single video often takes minutes, so a separate limit makes sense; the daily image limit above is still used for images.

video_cooldown.hint: Video-specific cooldown; the cooldown above is still used for images.

nsfw_filter.hint: Descriptions that match the word list are blocked outright (silent by default; enable the notice below). Both the user's wording and the AI-rewritten prompt are checked.

nsfw_words.description: Content filter word list (one per line, empty = built-in)
nsfw_words.hint: Leave empty to use the built-in generic list; once filled, the built-in list plus your entries apply. Case-insensitive.

nsfw_negative.description: Negative words added while the content filter is on
nsfw_negative.hint: For example `nsfw, nude, explicit`; appended to the negative prompt only while the content filter is on, to reduce borderline results.

nsfw_notify.description: Notify the user when the content filter blocks a request
nsfw_notify.hint: Off by default (silently ignored, consistent with the feature switches); when on, it replies “blocked by the content filter”.

audit_log.hint: Records every generation (who/when/purpose/which model/elapsed time/first 60 characters of the prompt) and content-filter blocks. Administrators view it with /audit [count] [--user ID]; the config-page API is at /audit. The file is audit.jsonl in the plugin data directory and keeps only the latest 2000 entries.

agent.description: Instruction-free generation (let the chat model call the drawing capability directly)

enable_llm_tool.hint: When on, users can simply say “draw me a …” to get an image without typing /draw. The model in use must support tool calling (function calling).

help.body:
🎨 ComfyUI Smart Drawing
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
/draw <description>  draw from one sentence
  inline options: 16:9 / --size 1024x1536 / --seed 42
                  --steps 30 / --cfg 6 / --lora name:0.8
                  --model keyword / --batch 2 / --negative "..."
            --llm force AI prompt rewrite / --no-llm skip it this time
/i2i      repaint from a photo (--denoise controls strength)
/outpaint extend the canvas (--left/--right/--top/--bottom px)
/video    text-to-video (--seconds / --fps / --length)
/i2v      animate a photo (send two photos = first → last frame)
/prompt   reverse-engineer a prompt from an image (--draw to draw at once, --detail for analysis)
/models   list available models
/templates list workflow templates (custom ones supported)
/status   ComfyUI connection and queue
/cancel   cancel your queued/running job (admin: /cancel all)
/audit     view audit log (admin, optional --user ID)
/inspect   model inspection: duplicates / misplaced / unused (admin)
/health    environment health check: flags / memory / template deps (admin)
/stats    usage statistics
/refresh-models  re-read the model list (admin)
/help     show this help

llm.completion_rule_commission: commission: without changing the **subject count / appearance / outfit style / action / setting type**, you may add 1-3 **presentation-layer** details (light direction and texture, material, composition and depth of field, mood) and list each one in added (one sentence each).
llm.completion_rule_strict: strict: draw only what I described. You may fill in necessary gaps such as aspect ratio and lighting, but do NOT add characters, clothing, props or setting elements; leave added as an empty array.
llm.optimize_system:
You are a ComfyUI prompt engineer: rewrite the user's description into English tag prompts that are ready to render, and pick models from the given list.
[Rewrite]
1. **Stay faithful**: only render what the user actually described. The **detail level** comes from the [Detail level] line in the user message — in strict mode do NOT invent characters, clothing, props or settings (only fill in genuinely blank areas: aspect, lighting, composition, and keep it restrained); in commission mode you may add a few presentation-layer details and must report them in added.
2. English, comma-separated, all lowercase. No sentences, no explanations, no numbering.
3. 15-30 tags. Too few fails to describe the scene; too many dilutes each tag's weight.
4. Cover all seven slots — subject (count and type), setting and environment, action and state, detail (material, texture, colour), lighting and mood, style and medium, quality words (rule 7) — but only write what is really there; skip what you cannot tell, never invent content to fill a slot (rule 1). Order (earliest matters most): subject count and type (1girl, solo / 2girls / no humans / landscape) → appearance (hair colour and style, eye colour, expression, gaze) → clothing and accessories → detail (material, texture, colour) → action and hand pose → camera angle and framing → setting → lighting and mood → art style and medium.
5. Give the hands a concrete action (hands on hips, holding a cup, arms crossed, hand on own cheek) — a specific hand to draw beats piling on negative tags afterwards.
6. Render Chinese proper nouns in their standard Danbooru form: 初音未来 → hatsune miku, 水墨 → ink painting.
7. Who writes the quality words depends on the [Quality words] line in the user message: when it does not ask you to, do NOT emit generic quality tags (masterpiece, best quality, 8k, ultra detailed, highres) — the plugin adds the right ones for the checkpoint's architecture, so yours would be duplicates; when it does ask, write 2-4 quality words specific to this image (e.g. film grain, soft bokeh), never a long list.
8. Do not use (word:1.2) weight syntax, and never put negative tags into positive.
[Negative]
9. Only put flaws specific to this description in negative; the plugin already adds generic hand/limb avoidance tags, so do not repeat them.
10. Leave it an empty string when nothing specific applies.
[Model picking]
11. Copy checkpoint filenames from the list verbatim — never invent, re-case or add paths. Match the style: photo-like/realistic → realistic checkpoint; anime/illustration → anime checkpoint. Filenames usually carry the hint (realvis / realistic / photo / juggernaut lean realistic, animagine / anything / anime / pony / illustrious lean anime); if unsure, use the first one in the list.
12. Only fill lora when its name clearly matches the user's subject or style, otherwise leave it an empty string; lora_strength is usually 0.6-0.9, use 0.8 if unsure.
13. Leave vae as an empty string.
[Output style]
14. Look at the checkpoint YOU picked and let it decide how positive is written; report that choice faithfully in prompt_style:
· A checkpoint whose name contains qwen-image (Qwen-Image and friends — the text encoder is an LLM) → set prompt_style to "natural" and write positive as fluent English sentences (1-3 sentences, 40-80 words) that walk through the seven slots in this order: subject → setting and environment → action and state → detail → lighting and mood → style and medium (quality words: rule 7). Do NOT pile up comma tags, do NOT use ((emphasis)).
· Any other checkpoint (SD1.5 / SDXL / Pony / Flux …) → set prompt_style to "tags" and write positive as English tags per rules 2-4 above.
[Output]
15. Output exactly one JSON object: no markdown fence, no prose before or after, no comments, no extra fields.
{"positive": "...", "negative": "...", "checkpoint": "...", "lora": "", "lora_strength": 0.8, "vae": "", "width": 0, "height": 0, "prompt_style": "tags", "added": []}
added lists the presentation-layer details YOU added beyond the user's description (only allowed in commission mode), one sentence each, at most 3 items; it must be an empty array in strict mode.
llm.quality_rule_llm: write 2-4 quality words specific to this image (e.g. film grain, soft bokeh); the plugin's generic ones are still merged in and duplicates are dropped.
llm.quality_rule_plugin: you do NOT write them — the plugin adds the checkpoint-appropriate generic ones.
llm.reverse_detail_system:
You are an illustration prompt reverse-engineer and image analyst: look at the image and output English tag prompts ready for Stable Diffusion, plus a Chinese analysis (composition / light / style / suspect areas).
[Looking at the image]
1. Describe only what is actually there. Do not guess patterns or accessories you cannot make out — an invented tag pushes the re-render away from the original.
2. Ignore artist signatures, watermarks, platform badges and any text in the frame: they are not image content and must not become tags.
3. Decide which kind of image it is first, then choose your vocabulary:
· Anime/illustration → Danbooru-style tags plus style and medium (anime, cel shading, watercolor)
· Real photograph → photographic description (photo, realistic, 35mm photograph), subject as woman / man / person; do NOT emit 1girl / anime tags
· No people → focus on setting and light, use no humans / landscape
[positive]
4. English, comma-separated, all lowercase, 15-45 tags, in this order: image type and subject count → appearance (hair colour and style, eye colour, expression, gaze) → clothing and accessories → action and hand pose (hands on hips, holding a cup, arms crossed) → camera angle and framing (from above, upper body, full body, close-up) → setting → lighting and mood → art style and medium.
5. Do not emit generic quality tags (masterpiece, best quality, 8k) — the plugin adds them per checkpoint when rendering.
[negative]
6. Only include flaws specific to this image (multi-person framing → extra limbs; a real photo → anime style); the plugin already adds generic hand/limb avoidance tags, so do not repeat them.
7. Leave it an empty string when nothing specific applies.
[summary]
8. Summarise the image in one Chinese sentence: subject + what they are doing + setting and light.
[analysis]
9. Analyse in Chinese, four blocks, 1-2 sentences each, max 80 characters per block; only what you can see — write "cannot tell" instead of guessing:
· composition: framing (subject placement, leading lines, depth, negative space)
· lighting: key light direction, warm / cool contrast, sources, palette
· style: medium, finish, style cues; do NOT name a specific model or artist
· anomalies: broken structure (fingers, limbs, objects), perspective drift, pseudo-text or watermarks; one sentence each, max 5, EMPTY array when none — never invent problems
[Output]
10. Output exactly one JSON object: no fence, no prose, no comments.
{"positive": "...", "negative": "...", "summary": "...", "analysis": {"composition": "...", "lighting": "...", "style": "...", "anomalies": ["..."]}}

llm.video_system:
You are an AI video prompt engineer. Rewrite the user's description as a VIDEO prompt, not image tags.
Rules:
1. Spell out the action: who does what, and how it changes (e.g. "slowly turns her head", "body sways gently", "looks into the camera").
2. Specify exactly one camera move: static / slow push-in / lateral pan / slight handheld.
3. Cover the scene as "subject + look and clothing → environment → lighting and mood", one or two sentences each; do not pile up adjectives.
4. Keep the user's language: if they wrote Chinese, answer in Chinese (Wan models understand Chinese natively).
5. 40-80 Chinese characters (or 25-50 English words).
6. Never write "static", "motionless", "video" or "frame", and do not name models or parameters.
7. Do not emit generic quality tags (masterpiece, best quality, 8k, 4k); the plugin already adds generic quality and deformity-avoidance tags, so do not repeat them in negative.
8. Output JSON only: {"positive": "the rewritten prompt", "negative": "one image-specific negative tag, or an empty string"}; keep negative to the one or two flaws that matter here.
Output JSON only, no explanation.

text.001: ComfyUI address reachable from the machine running AstrBot.
text.002: Ask ComfyUI to free VRAM/RAM before switching model families (video <-> SDXL). On 16G machines this avoids the os error 1455 crash. On by default.
text.003: With several ComfyUI instances jobs go to the least busy one; a failing backend is temporarily skipped. Leave empty for a single backend.
text.004: Limit concurrent generations; extra requests queue with their position shown.
text.005: Read straight from ComfyUI's model folders. Only models listed here are used.
text.006: Loaded automatically when you open this tab.
text.007: Use an LLM to rewrite the description and pick a checkpoint/LoRA from the real model list.
text.008: When off, your text is used as-is with the first available checkpoint; no LLM needed.
text.009: When on, /video and /i2v first rewrite your text into a **video prompt**: it adds the motion (slowly turning her head, gentle swaying), one camera move (static / push-in / pan) and the lighting mood, while keeping your language (Chinese stays Chinese - Wan understands it). Unlike images (English tags), video wants natural-language action. The model comes from the "default t2v / i2v model" fields below - the AI only rewrites the prompt. Override per message with --llm / --no-llm.
text.010: /reverse needs a vision-capable model. Without it AstrBot replaces the image with "[Image]" and the model invents content.
text.011: Add a vision model (qwen-vl-max, glm-4v, gpt-4o, ...) in AstrBot's providers and put its ID here.
text.012: When a base URL is set, the provider above is ignored.
text.013: Test another model without editing config: /reverse --provider <id>. /status shows the active vision model.
text.014: Resolution, CFG and sampler are adapted to the checkpoint architecture (SD1.5 / SDXL / Pony / Flux).
text.015: When off, the values below are only fallbacks for unknown architectures.
text.016: Quality tags are added for SD1.5 / Pony, not for SDXL / Flux.
text.018: Send an image with a description to redraw it; /img2img works with just an image too.
text.019: When off, attached images fall back to text-to-image; /img2img still works explicitly.
text.020: Denoise: 0.3 touches details, 0.6 (default) changes style, 0.8+ almost redraws. Size follows the source aspect ratio, aligned to 8.
text.021: Generate small, then upscale and redraw. Best for hands/faces/details; roughly doubles the time.
text.022: Every /draw runs an extra upscale pass.
text.024: When on, users may pass --hires 1.5 or --hires 0; when off your settings always win.
text.025: Final size = original x factor, aligned to 8. On 8GB cards keep the factor at or below 1.5.
text.026: Generate short videos with /video; needs video models and nodes installed in ComfyUI (e.g. Wan 2.x).
text.027: The tier caps resolution / frames / steps: low 480p, <=97 frames, <=12 steps; mid 720p, <=121, <=30; high 720p, <=161, <=50. Auto detects VRAM and drops a tier below 20G RAM. On low/mid tiers an unnamed model prefers files containing turbo / lightning / distill / schnell (measured: Turbo 4 steps = 74 s vs 20 steps = 281 s). Filling a model name above always wins.
text.028: When off, only the local file path is sent (for platforms that cannot play video).
text.029: Images are pruned by age and count to protect disk space.
text.030: Mention the requester when drawing in a group.
text.031: Show template, checkpoint, size, seed and time for reproducibility.
text.032: Live "step n / total" over ComfyUI's WebSocket; falls back to polling without affecting the result.
text.033: Upload an image, paint over what should change (red), write a description, then run inpaint. The mask is built in your browser only.
text.034: No result yet. Upload an image, paint a mask, then run inpaint.
text.035: Admin rights come from AstrBot itself; here you only maintain lists and limits.
text.036: When off, admins are limited too (the blacklist always wins).
text.037: Record every generation (who/when/purpose/model/time/first 60 chars) and content-filter blocks; admins read it with /audit.
text.038: Feature names: t2i / i2i / outpaint / inpaint / t2v / i2v / reverse_prompt, or all / none. Priority: user > group > default > the feature switches under Advanced.
text.039: Prompts matching the word list are blocked; both the raw text and the AI-rewritten prompt are checked.
text.040: Off by default (silent, like feature switches); when on the user gets a short notice.
text.041: This language drives both the plugin page and chat messages.
text.042: Only text-to-image is on by default. Disabled features are silently ignored (no reply) and cost no VRAM; the LLM tool obeys this too.
text.044: Image-to-image uses more VRAM and can edit others' images; enable deliberately.
text.045: Extend the canvas outwards; VRAM grows with the margin.
text.046: Redraw a painted region; the Inpaint tab reports it as unavailable when off.
text.047: Heaviest feature: 74-281 s per clip on an 8G card.
text.048: Animate a still (two images = first/last frame). Also VRAM heavy.
text.049: Not generation strictly speaking, but it calls a vision model, so it has a switch too.
text.050: Let the chat model call the drawing tool when the user says "draw me ...".
text.051: Requires tool calling; the drawing tool is exposed to the chat model when on.
text.053: Model inspection (duplicates / misplaced / unused) plus an environment health check (flags / memory / template dependencies).
text.054: Click "Run inspection" to build the report.
text.055: Built-in templates are picked by architecture; drop API-format JSON into the custom folder to add one.
text.056: Generation counts, model usage and a gallery.
text.057: Pack the parameter text and images into a single forwarded message — no more spamming when one request produces several images (QQ personal account / OneBot v11 only). Falls back to normal sending when the platform is not aiocqhttp, the result is a video, or the images exceed 20MB in total.
text.058: With llm the plugin's generic words are still merged in and duplicates are dropped; to hand quality words to the AI entirely, turn off "auto quality tags per checkpoint" above.
text.059: Commission mode relaxes "do not invent", but only for presentation-layer details (light and texture, material, composition and depth of field, mood) and never changes subject count / appearance / outfit style / action / setting type; whatever it added is listed in the result. Override once with /draw … --commission or --strict.
text.060: Off by default. When on, commission mode makes a gentle adjustment — only if you did not specify the parameter yourself: SD family CFG ×0.85 (never below 1.5), Flux family guidance −1.0 (never below 1.0). Inline --cfg and configured defaults always win.
